narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Game Night Arcade"**

Blackjack Party looks like a friendly board game crossed with an arcade cabinet. Every surface is a thick, toy-like object: a cream or candy-colored face, a 3px night-ink outline, and a hard offset shadow with no blur that makes it sit up off the page. The table itself is a big, flat felt-green stage with an orange rail, drawn in the same outlined style, so the Angular controls around it and the PixiJS scene read as one world.

Color is bright and plentiful but always has a job. Each table action owns a color (Hit green, Stand red, Double lemon, Split blue). Chips are coded by value. Results are coded by outcome. A shared ink color holds it all together. Type is loud where it labels the game (Lilita One for headings, buttons, pills and every word on the felt) and plain where it explains (Nunito, set bold throughout so it holds up next to the chunky display face).

Density is generous. Controls are large, easy to hit and easy to read across a room or on a landscape phone. Playfulness lives in shape, color and motion, never in hiding the game state.
keyCharacteristics: 3px night-ink outlines on every raised element, matched by 4–8px ink strokes in the canvas
Hard offset drop shadows (6px or 3px straight down, no blur) instead of soft elevation
Big radii and pill shapes: nothing is sharp-cornered
One color per meaning: actions, chip values and hand results each have a fixed color
A warm sand page with large soft color blobs and a faint dot grid behind the content

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: A game color always means the same thing everywhere: Hit is always green, Stand always red, $100 is always blue, in the HUD and on the felt. Never reuse an action or chip color for decoration.

rules.name: The Theme File Rule
rules.body: UI colors are defined only in `theme.css` and the canvas palette only in `palette.ts`. Components use semantic names (`primary`, `neutral`, `--color-felt`), never raw values.

rules.name: The Display Speaks for the Game Rule
rules.body: Anything a player acts on or watches (buttons, pills, banners, totals, results) is set in Lilita One. Explanations and conversation stay in Nunito.

rules.name: The Always Bold Rule
rules.body: Body text is bold by default (`font-bold` on `body`). Don't set regular-weight running text next to the display face.

rules.name: The Always Chunky Rule
rules.body: Every raised surface gets the 3px ink border plus a hard offset shadow. No soft or blurred shadows and no glass effects on surfaces. The one existing exception is the collapsed chat/log toggle, which is see-through on purpose so it stays out of the way over the felt.

rules.name: The Flat When Disabled Rule
rules.body: Disabled controls lose their shadow and outline strength and get a solid toasted sand face. They sink; they never just fade out.

dos: Do give every raised element the 3px night-ink border and one of the two hard shadows (`chunky` / `chunky-sm`).
Do keep each game color tied to one meaning: Hit green, Stand red, Double lemon, Split blue; chips $5 red, $25 green, $100 blue, $500 grape.
Do set anything actionable or game-state in Lilita One, and keep explanatory text in bold Nunito.
Do add new colors only in `theme.css`, and mirror any change the canvas needs in `palette.ts`.
Do give disabled controls a solid toasted sand face so they stay readable over the felt.
Do use pills and circles for status, badges, chips and avatars, and 0.9–1.4rem corners for everything else.
donts: Don't use soft or blurred box shadows, glassmorphism or gradient surfaces on controls and cards.
Don't use sharp corners or hairline (1px) borders on raised elements.
Don't reuse an action, chip or result color for decoration.
Don't hard-code color values in components; use the semantic theme names.
Don't name component classes after DaisyUI components (`title`, `status`); use names like `table-title` or `status-bar`.
